notes:
Account snapshot and POC scope.

- Company background: Codex Replicant Systems (CRS) builds an IDE-native copilot targeting enterprise engineering teams (on-prem CI/CD, heavy compliance). 300+ devs, monorepo at scale.
- Primary ask: deterministic, reproducible code completions across dev teams with safe rollouts. Key features requested: model/version pinning per workspace, canary rollouts by team, eval gates before global rollout, and low-latency streaming to preserve typing experience.
- Performance targets: 30-50ms token latency for inline completion, p95 < 80ms for short completions, ~8000 reqs/s peak for org-wide runs. Cost sensitivity: wants clear unit economics for dedicated pools.
- Quality/reproducibility metrics CRS cares about: compilation rate of generated code, unit-test pass rate on small snippets, exact-match for boilerplate, and API-stability (no behavior drift across pinned versions). They want automated eval gates that compare model candidate vs baseline on canonical prompt set.
- Security/compliance: must support SSO/SAML, tenant-level audit logs, KMS integration for key management, and EU data residency for some customers. Also want an air-gapped option for a regulated client (future phase).
- POC plan (agreed verbally 2026-02-20):
  * Week 0: deploy hosted POC with pinned model variant and telemetry hooks.
  * Week 1: run synthetic eval set (1.5k prompts) to establish baseline metrics (compile rate, unit-test proxy).
  * Week 2: run canary rollout to 2 internal teams (5% traffic) with automatic eval gate — if metrics regress >2% vs baseline, auto-rollback.
  * Deliverable: evaluation report + recommended batching/quantization profile for Dedicated.
- Notes from conversations: SE noted "need deterministic outputs when pinning across workspaces — non-determinism breaks CI". Eng lead: "we'll need a rollback window and tight observability — token-level diffing would be ideal".
- Risks flagged: quantized models may lower compile-rate; need to define acceptable thresholds up-front. Legal wants explicit data residency addendum for EU customers.
- Linked artifacts: pricing deck in Drive (sent 2026-02-22), security questionnaire in Drive (answers partial), Fireflies for demo (ff_20260214_2310).
- Internal Redwood asks: have sample eval prompt set (500-1500 prompts) that cover imports, small functions, and edge-case macros. Requesting test harness for running unit-test proxies on completions.

Short next actions (from AE):
- Schedule POC kick-off with Eng + SE for 2026-03-15.
- Deliver sample eval repo + harness by 2026-03-09.
- Follow up with Legal on data residency clause; connect to Partner Ops for Dedicated pricing model.

Quote from Eng lead (paraphrase): "If we can pin model versions and automate canary gates that mirror our CI checks, we'll standardize code completions across teams and avoid mystery regressions."
